title: Same energy, different tariff
hook: Moving a hypothetical load changes its price while leaving its energy unchanged.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Distinguish a cost change from an energy-use change.

misconception: A lower electricity charge necessarily means fewer kilowatt-hours were used.
objective: Distinguish a cost change from an energy-use change.

claims.text: The same 3kWh is billed at fictional rates of €0.40/kWh or €0.20/kWh, with no other charges. Scaled model; fictional:€0.40/kWh-or-€0.20/kWh;same kWh.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Energy=3kWh, A=€1.2 and B=€0.6. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x",0.4]; B=["*","x",0.2]; x denotes Energy. At x=3, A=1.2, B=0.6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The cost changes because the price multiplier changes. The energy quantity stays the same. This isolates tariff arithmetic and does not imply that every load can safely or practically move to another time.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x",0.4]; B=["*","x",0.2]; x denotes Energy. At x=3, A=1.2, B=0.6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A modeled bill falls from €2.40 to €1.20 because the same use moved from a fictional €0.40/kWh rate to €0.20/kWh. How much energy was used each time? Correct: 6kWh both times. €2.40 ÷ €0.40 = 6kWh and €1.20 ÷ €0.20 = 6kWh: the price changed, the energy did not.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x",0.4]; B=["*","x",0.2]; x denotes Energy. At x=3, A=1.2, B=0.6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, company/reviews/lifehacks-200/recall-patch-resources.lines.txt), applied 2026-10-14 by demo-builder; c4 restates the new recall item.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff.

claims.text: Tariffs and appliance ratings vary: check your own.
claims.source: Safety-required stage line (company/reviews/lh-same-energy-new-tariff/2026-10-14-safety.md, lifehacks-safety-reviewer). Source owed: a national energy body or tariff regulator guidance, to be found and checked by the fact-checker. The reviewer named none, and none is asserted here.

recall.question: A modeled bill falls from €2.40 to €1.20 because the same use moved from a fictional €0.40/kWh rate to €0.20/kWh. How much energy was used each time?
recall.why: €2.40 ÷ €0.40 = 6kWh and €1.20 ÷ €0.20 = 6kWh: the price changed, the energy did not.
